memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh's gate 8, when selected via --only-gate N, runs its OWN internal UNFLAGGED full run-all.sh sweep (all suites) under the specs/.gate-lock mutex rather than a scoped subset. Under a Batch Gate Deferral directive (or any scoped-verification intent), never include gate 8 in --only-gate; cover its content instead with a separate run-all.sh --only SUITE[,...] invocation, which does not touch specs/.gate-lock for a narrowed run.

bash's `read -r a b < <(cmd)` reads only ONE line from the process substitution and splits it by IFS into the named variables -- it does not read successive output lines into successive variables. To capture several output lines from one command substitution into separate variables, use `mapfile -t arr < <(cmd)` and index into the array.

`grep -c PATTERN FILE 2>/dev/null || echo 0` can print TWO lines when FILE exists and has zero matches: grep prints '0' to stdout on a clean zero-match run but still exits 1, which also triggers the `|| echo 0` fallback, yielding '0\n0' where a single integer was expected downstream (e.g. in a `[ "$n" -eq 0 ]` test). Capture grep's own stdout via `n="$(grep -c ...)" || true; echo "${n:-0}"` instead of appending a bare `|| echo 0` fallback after a `-c` count.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-deploy.sh gate 8 --only-gate selection hazard
sapience_notes.value: Selecting gate 8 via verify-deploy.sh --only-gate N triggers the script's own internal UNFLAGGED full run-all.sh sweep (all suites) under the specs/.gate-lock mutex, rather than a scoped subset -- this defeats scoped-verification intent and can stall for minutes. The correct scoped substitute for gate 8's content is a separate run-all.sh --only SUITE[,...] invocation, which does not touch specs/.gate-lock for a narrowed run. Never include gate 8 in a --only-gate list when trying to avoid a full sweep.

sapience_notes.subject: bash read vs mapfile for multi-line command substitution
sapience_notes.value: bash's `read -r a b < <(cmd)` only reads ONE line and splits it by IFS into the named variables; it does not read successive lines into successive variables. To capture multiple output lines from a process substitution into separate variables, use `mapfile -t arr < <(cmd)` and index into the array.

sapience_notes.subject: grep -c with an || fallback can double-print on a clean zero-match run
sapience_notes.value: `grep -c PATTERN FILE 2>/dev/null || echo 0` can print TWO lines when FILE exists and has zero matches: grep itself prints '0' to stdout but still exits 1 (no match found), which also triggers the `|| echo 0` fallback. Capture grep's own stdout via `n="$(grep -c ...)" || true; echo "${n:-0}"` instead.

sapience_notes.subject: deploy-root-guard.sh constrains live attestation of new core/extension scripts
sapience_notes.value: A newly-written script that sources deploy-root-guard.sh (the standard pattern for core/extension scripts) refuses to run from the agent-system source store -- it must be smoke-tested either against a scratch deployed-tree-shaped fixture (copy the script plus its sibling dependencies into <scratch>/.claude/scripts/) or, for the real thing, only after deploy-headless.sh has actually run. Plan a phase's own verification section accordingly: a literal source-store invocation named in a plan's Verification bullet will not execute as written pre-deploy.

sapience_notes.subject: A seed-class enum can accumulate silent duplicate copies across a codebase
sapience_notes.value: A single open/extensible enum (issue-record.sh's seed-class list) had, prior to this task, THREE independently-maintained copies across the codebase (issue-log.md's doc table, issue-record.sh's own comment+array, and orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh's separate SEED_CLASSES_JSON for conclusion-stage tallying) plus at least four more loose count-reference strings scattered across unrelated files, none updated in lockstep historically. When growing such an enum, grep the whole repo for every count-reference string before editing; never trust a plan's own named file list as exhaustive.
